# Project Governance 4.5.0

Native prompts now deliver required guidance and current task facts without automatically indexing optional source or calling JEV. An attached repository does not imply a request to search it.

Explicit context retrieval defaults to local search. Use `context-route --task <request> --retrieval semantic` when bounded paid selection is useful. Existing sharing permissions, source freshness, model settings, original turn expiry and total spending limits still apply. Local requests consume no paid continuation. Unmatched files no longer fill otherwise empty results.

Passive context telemetry now reports requested and effective modes, skipped index work, linked native-entry coverage, missing usage/read/outcome evidence, and deduplicated cache-aware token subtotals. `telemetry context status --since <ISO timestamp>` limits the inspected capture period. Returned context is not proof of model consumption or accepted work.

This is a deliberate minor adoption change from 4.4.3. Existing profiles remain valid. Provider-job context also defaults to local retrieval. Publication does not upgrade any project or worktree.

Qualification uses the normal 4.x local source and exact installed-archive path, with independent reviews and offline provider fixtures. Controlled tests do not establish live host consumption, accepted development savings or an account-wide daily spending ceiling. Compare matched accepted tasks before claiming economic benefit. A shared monetary cap and a passage-only experimental mode remain separate proposals.
